access_type_at_launch: Invite-only Early Access riders via Robotaxi app; in-car safety monitor in front passenger seat (not a driver); ~10-20 Model Y vehicles; flat $4.20 promotional fare
current_status: Active; expanding geofence and fleet; Tesla's purpose-built Cybercab entered commercial service here in Sept 2026
notes: Musk said launch would start with ~10 vehicles (CNBC 2025-06-20/22). Fleet grew and safety monitors began moving from front passenger seat to trailing chase car and then some vehicles went fully unsupervised starting ~2025-12 to 2026-01 (Electrek/CNBC 2026-01-22). Musk's stated goal of 500 vehicles by end of 2025 was not met (Electrek 2025-11-26, "slashes fleet goal from 500 to ~60"). Geofence grew from an ~18-20 sq mi launch footprint (DriveTeslaCanada retrospective) to ~243-245 sq mi by 2025-10-28 (supervised/app-wide service area; DriveTeslaCanada), then the UNSUPERVISED service was extended to match that full ~245 sq mi footprint on 2026-06-03 covering Pflugerville, Manor, Gigafactory Texas and the airport (CleanTechnica 2026-06-03). NHTSA opened an informal inquiry within a day of the June 2025 launch after erratic-driving videos surfaced (CNBC 2025-06-23); CBS News reported 14 crashes since launch as of its report. UPDATE 2026-09-23 (re-verified): geofence expanded again ~9% on/around 2026-08-31 to ~264 sq mi (NotATeslaApp, citing 244->264 sq mi and growth toward Pflugerville along US-183/I-35), while a same-week TeslaOracle/Statesman report described the post-expansion area as ~288 sq mi -- treat 264-288 sq mi as the current range, both describing the same Aug-2026 expansion. Tesla held an invite-only Cybercab launch event at ACL Live in Austin on 2026-09-03 (Musk did not attend; no livestream materialized per Forbes/Motor1), and paid Cybercab rides began in a limited part of Austin on 2026-09-04. Cybercab TX DMV registrations jumped from 7 to 45 within the launch week (Teslarati), and Tesla's TX-statewide (Austin+Dallas+Houston) registered AV count reached 420 (375 Model Y + 45 Cybercab) as of 2026-09-02 (NextBigFuture/texasavtracker.com), vs Waymo's 988 in TX the same date. NHTSA opened Audit Query AQ26002 into Tesla's FMVSS self-certification of the Cybercab on 2026-09-03 (same day as the Austin launch) -- examining how a vehicle with no steering wheel/pedals/mirrors was certified -- and escalated it to a formal Special Order on 2026-09-10, with Tesla's response due 2026-09-30 (NHTSA press release; TechCrunch; Electrek 2026-09-04). Tesla announced Robotaxi crossed 1,000,000 cumulative UNSUPERVISED miles on 2026-09-03, up from 380,000 miles at the 2026-07-22 Q2 2026 earnings call (~620,000 miles added in ~6 weeks); Teslarati reported ~200 vehicles now operating unsupervised across Austin/Dallas/Houston combined, with zero notable safety incidents claimed to date (Electrek 2026-09-03).

access_type_at_launch: Invite-only for select Tesla owners via Robotaxi app; human safety driver in driver's seat (required under CA DMV testing permit, not a driverless deployment)
current_status: Active but small-scale; safety driver still legally required as of 2026-09; CPUC continues to state Tesla is not operating an autonomous vehicle service
notes: Tesla only holds a CPUC transportation charter-party carrier (TCP) permit plus a CA DMV permit to test with a safety driver; CPUC has confirmed Tesla has NOT applied for the driverless/autonomous passenger service authorization needed to run an actual robotaxi in CA (CNBC 2025-07-25; ABC7 2025-07/2025). Geofence spans from north of the Golden Gate Bridge to San Jose, with invite-only rides confirmed in San Francisco, Berkeley, Oakland, Hayward, Fremont and San Jose specifically (NotATeslaApp 2025-07-25/2962; DriveTeslaCanada). Musk stated at the Q4 2025 earnings call (2026-01-28) that the combined Austin+Bay Area fleet was "well over 500" vehicles, but this is not broken out by geography. Independent tracker (Robotaxi Tracker, via Electrek) put active Bay Area fleet at ~107-168 vehicles in April 2026, collapsing to ~9 active by late May 2026 (Electrek 2026-05-26). UPDATE 2026-09-23 (re-verified): no geofence expansion or fleet-size disclosure specific to the Bay Area was found since July 2026. Electrek (2026-03-25) reported CPUC stating plainly that "Tesla is not operating an autonomous vehicle service" in California and holds only the same charter-party-carrier permit a limousine company gets, with no AV safety reporting or quarterly filings; CPUC further indicated Tesla will not receive a CA AV permit before the end of 2026 and has not applied for one (evxl.co 2026-03-27, corroborating). For competitive context, Waymo won CPUC approval on 2026-08-14 to expand across 18 California counties (Electrek), underscoring the regulatory gap between the two companies' Bay Area status.

current_status: Active; unsupervised; fleet and geofence both growing
official_fleet_size: unknown (city-specific figure never disclosed by Tesla)
notes: Announced as part of a 7-city 1H-2026 expansion list (Dallas, Houston, Phoenix, Miami, Orlando, Tampa, Las Vegas) in Tesla's Q4 2025 shareholder deck released with Q4 2025 earnings on 2026-01-28 (Teslarati). Launched with Houston on 2026-04-18, four days ahead of Tesla's Q1 2026 earnings report (mlq.ai; NotATeslaApp #4004; Electrek 2026-04-18). Initial geofence ~30-35 sq mi (~31 sq mi per later retrospective reporting). Texas DMV (SB 2807) registration data (a state regulatory record, not a Tesla-disclosed per-city number) showed Tesla's statewide TX fleet (Austin+Dallas+Houston combined) at 42 vehicles as of 2026-05-28, versus Waymo's 577 (TechCrunch 2026-05-28); that statewide TX count reportedly grew to ~175 by 2026-07-03 (Benzinga), then to 420 (375 Model Y + 45 Cybercab) by 2026-09-02 vs Waymo's 988 (NextBigFuture/texasavtracker.com). Independent tracker reports put Dallas-specific unsupervised count at ~5 (2026-05-13, CleanTechnica) then ~3 (2026-05-26, Electrek). UPDATE 2026-09-23 (re-verified): Dallas geofence more than doubled on/around 2026-08-29, from ~31 sq mi to ~81 sq mi (a ~158-161% increase), extending west toward Irving/US-183 and the I-30 corridor and south through downtown to I-35E (NotATeslaApp; TeslaOracle 2026-09-01). Every Dallas ride continues to run fully unsupervised (Teslaoracle 2026-09-20).

access_type_at_launch: Not yet launched as of 2026-09-23 (AVNC commercial permit APPROVED 2026-08-20/21; launch pending completion of administrative/regulatory steps)
current_status: Regulatory approval obtained (up to 5,000 vehicles authorized); commercial service has not yet begun; Tesla has a 120-day window from approval to begin operating
notes: Nevada DOT approved Tesla for AV testing in the Las Vegas Valley (~Sept 2025). Tesla Robotaxi LLC filed an Autonomous Vehicle Network Company (AVNC) permit application with the Nevada Transportation Authority (Docket 26-05015) on 2026-06-05, requesting authority for up to 5,000 vehicles in year one; public comment period ran through 2026-07-05 and the application was still in staff review as of 2026-07-22, with no approval yet announced (DriveTeslaCanada; Review-Journal; CDC Gaming; Basenor). Tesla has invested ~$3.1M in a Las Vegas depot at 6170 Mohawk St with 8 Superchargers and 6 car lifts, and holds 2 Clark County business licenses (auto wash/detailing; Fremont St admin office) (Review-Journal). Gold-colored Cybercabs have been spotted testing in Southern Nevada (TeslaNorth 2026-06-22). MAJOR UPDATE 2026-09-23 (re-verified): on 2026-08-20/21, the Nevada Transportation Authority UNANIMOUSLY APPROVED commercial AVNC permits for Tesla (up to 5,000 vehicles), Waymo (1,000) and Uber (1,000) to operate in Clark County (TechCrunch 2026-08-20; Engadget; GuruFocus; TeslaOracle 2026-08-21; Basenor). This is a regulatory green light, not a launch: all three companies must still complete vehicle inspections, insurance filings and rate approval, and have 120 days from the August approval (i.e., roughly by mid-to-late December 2026) to begin commercial operation; as of 2026-09-23 no company, including Tesla, had published a Las Vegas start date or begun paid rides (TechCrunch 2026-08-20; thechargeport.com, last verified 2026-09-05).

notes: Not part of Tesla's officially announced 7-city 1H-2026 expansion list. First surfaced in this research via the independent tracker open-robotaxi.vercel.app (lists New Orleans among cities "in testing or permitting phases" as of 2026-08-31). Confirmed independently: Model Ys with rear and side camera washers (the Robotaxi-specific hardware signature) and Texas manufacturer plates were spotted testing in New Orleans (NotATeslaApp #4408; X/@SawyerMerritt; Basenor). Regulatory status is an active obstacle, not just a Tesla timeline choice: per Axios New Orleans (2026-06-15, re: Waymo but describing the same citywide rule), New Orleans currently requires officials to pass a new ordinance before any driverless ride-hailing service (Waymo, Zoox, or Tesla Robotaxi) can operate commercially there, with the City Council expected to begin drafting that ordinance only in fall 2026. No Tesla launch-date announcement was found as of 2026-09-23; treat this row as low-confidence/speculative pending both a Tesla announcement and a City Council ordinance.
